# core/slots.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from core/slots.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

A growable table of numbered slots, for ids that a
program hands out and takes back (process ids, file descriptors, pipe
and socket numbers).

A `Slots[V]` is a vector of `Option[V]`: slot `i` is in use when it holds
`Some`. `slots_alloc` puts a value in the lowest free slot at or above a
starting id, growing the vector when every slot is in use, up to a limit
the caller gives (a process's `RLIMIT_NOFILE`, say). File descriptors
start the search at 0 (POSIX wants the lowest free one); process ids
start after the last one handed out, so that a fresh id is not one that
just died. Like `HashMap[V]`, `V` must be a type that can be copied; to
number linear values, keep them in a `Vec[T]` and store the index.

What is proved: every index is in bounds; `slots_alloc` returns a slot
that was free and now holds the value, at or above the starting id and
below the limit, and every slot between the starting id and it was in
use; a failed `slots_alloc` means every slot from the starting id up to
the limit is in use; growing never stops the program (when memory runs
out, `slots_alloc` says so and changes nothing); every function changes
no slot but the one it names.

`import "core/slots.bastio";` also loads [core/option.bastio](core-option.md).

| Function | |
| --- | --- |
| [`slots_new`](#slots_new) | A table with no slots. |
| [`slots_cap`](#slots_cap) | The number of slots, used or free. |
| [`slots_used`](#slots_used) | Is slot `i` in use? Any `i` may be asked. |
| [`slots_get`](#slots_get) | The value in slot `i`, if it is in use. |
| [`slots_set`](#slots_set) | Replaces the value in slot `i`, which must be in use. |
| [`slots_take`](#slots_take) | Frees slot `i` and returns what it held (`None` if it was free or past the end). |
| [`slots_find_free`](#slots_find_free) | The lowest free slot of `from..limit`, or `limit` when every one is in use. |
| [`slots_alloc`](#slots_alloc) | Puts `v` in the lowest free slot of `from..limit`, adding slots to the table when that slot is past its end. |
| [`slots_count`](#slots_count) | The number of slots in use. |
| [`slots_free`](#slots_free) | Frees the table. |

Every example below is built, verified and run by `tests/run.sh`. An `assert` in one is proved at compile time from the contracts above it.

## Types and constants

### `Slots`

```bastio
struct Slots[V] {
  vals: Vec[Option[V]],
}
```

### `SLOTS_NOMEM`

```bastio
const SLOTS_NOMEM: u64 = 18446744073709551615;
```

What `slots_alloc` returns when the table had to grow and memory ran
out. It is above every limit, so it is never a slot.

## Functions

### `slots_new`

```bastio
fn slots_new[V]() -> Slots[V]
  ensures vlen(result.vals) == 0
```

A table with no slots.

Example:

```bastio
// File descriptors: the lowest free one below a limit of 16.
let mut fds = slots_new[u64]();
let a = slots_alloc[u64](&mut fds, 0, 16, 100);   // 0
let b = slots_alloc[u64](&mut fds, 0, 16, 200);   // 1
if a >= 16 || b >= 16 { slots_free[u64](fds); return 1; }   // full or out of memory
assert slots_maps[u64](fds, b, 200);   // proved: slot b holds 200
let closed = slots_take[u64](&mut fds, a);   // close fd 0
let c = slots_alloc[u64](&mut fds, 0, 16, 300);   // reuses 0
let ok = a == 0 && b == 1 && c == 0 && opt_or[u64](closed, 0) == 100 && slots_count[u64](fds) == 2;
slots_free[u64](fds);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `slots_cap`

```bastio
fn slots_cap[V](s: &Slots[V]) -> u64
  ensures result == vlen(s.vals)
```

The number of slots, used or free. Ids at or past it are free.

### `slots_used`

```bastio
fn slots_used[V](s: &Slots[V], i: u64) -> bool
  ensures result == slots_has[V](s, i)
```

Is slot `i` in use? Any `i` may be asked.

### `slots_get`

```bastio
fn slots_get[V](s: &Slots[V], i: u64) -> Option[V]
  ensures (result is Option::Some) == slots_has[V](s, i)
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> slots_maps[V](s, i, result.Some)
```

The value in slot `i`, if it is in use. Any `i` may be asked.

Example:

```bastio
let mut s = slots_new[u64]();
let i = slots_alloc[u64](&mut s, 0, 8, 42);
let mut ok = i == 0;
if i < 8 {
  slots_set[u64](&mut s, i, 43);   // allowed: slot i is in use
  ok = ok && opt_or[u64](slots_get[u64](s, i), 0) == 43 && slots_used[u64](s, i);
}
// Any id may be asked: one past the end is simply free.
ok = ok && !slots_used[u64](s, 1000) && slots_get[u64](s, 1000) is Option::None;
ok = ok && slots_find_free[u64](s, 0, 8) == 1;
slots_free[u64](s);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `slots_set`

```bastio
fn slots_set[V](s: &mut Slots[V], i: u64, v: V)
  requires slots_has[V](s, i)
  ensures slots_maps[V](s, i, v) && vlen(s.vals) == vlen(old(s).vals)
  ensures slots_same_but[V](s, old(s), i)
```

Replaces the value in slot `i`, which must be in use.

### `slots_take`

```bastio
fn slots_take[V](s: &mut Slots[V], i: u64) -> Option[V]
  ensures !slots_has[V](s, i) && vlen(s.vals) == vlen(old(s).vals)
  ensures slots_same_but[V](s, old(s), i)
  ensures (result is Option::Some) == slots_has[V](old(s), i)
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> slots_maps[V](old(s), i, result.Some)
```

Frees slot `i` and returns what it held (`None` if it was free or past
the end).

### `slots_find_free`

```bastio
fn slots_find_free[V](s: &Slots[V], from: u64, limit: u64) -> u64
  requires from <= limit
  ensures from <= result && result <= limit
  ensures slots_full[V](s, from, result)
  ensures result < limit ==> !slots_has[V](s, result)
```

The lowest free slot of `from..limit`, or `limit` when every one is in
use. It may be at or past the end of the table.

### `slots_alloc`

```bastio
fn slots_alloc[V](s: &mut Slots[V], from: u64, limit: u64, v: V) -> u64
  requires from <= limit && limit <= 1152921504606846976
  ensures result == SLOTS_NOMEM || (from <= result && result <= limit)
  ensures result != SLOTS_NOMEM ==> slots_full[V](old(s), from, result)
  ensures result < limit ==> !slots_has[V](old(s), result) && slots_maps[V](s, result, v)
  ensures result < limit && result < vlen(old(s).vals) ==> vlen(s.vals) == vlen(old(s).vals)
  ensures result < limit && vlen(old(s).vals) <= result ==> vlen(s.vals) == result + 1
  ensures result >= limit ==> vlen(s.vals) == vlen(old(s).vals)
  ensures slots_same_but[V](s, old(s), result)
```

Puts `v` in the lowest free slot of `from..limit`, adding slots to the
table when that slot is past its end. Returns the slot; `limit` when
every slot of `from..limit` is in use; or `SLOTS_NOMEM` when the table
had to grow and memory ran out. It never stops the program, and on
either failure `s` is unchanged.

Example:

```bastio
// A full range and the two failures, which change nothing.
let mut s = slots_new[u64]();
let x = slots_alloc[u64](&mut s, 0, 2, 1);
let y = slots_alloc[u64](&mut s, 0, 2, 2);
let z = slots_alloc[u64](&mut s, 0, 2, 3);   // 0 and 1 are in use: the limit, 2
// Process ids: search from just past the last one handed out.
let p = slots_alloc[u64](&mut s, 5, 32, 9);   // 5: slots 2..4 are added free
let ok = x == 0 && y == 1 && z == 2 && p == 5 && slots_cap[u64](s) == 6 && z != SLOTS_NOMEM;
slots_free[u64](s);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `slots_count`

```bastio
fn slots_count[V](s: &Slots[V]) -> u64
  ensures result <= vlen(s.vals)
```

The number of slots in use.

### `slots_free`

```bastio
fn slots_free[V](s: Slots[V])
```

Frees the table. Values that own nothing are simply dropped.

## Specification functions

### `slots_has`

```bastio
spec fn slots_has[V](s: &Slots[V], i: u64) -> bool {
  i < vlen(s.vals) && vget(s.vals, i) is Option::Some
}
```

Slot `i` exists and is in use.

### `slots_maps`

```bastio
spec fn slots_maps[V](s: &Slots[V], i: u64, v: V) -> bool {
  slots_has[V](s, i) && vget(s.vals, i).Some == v
}
```

Slot `i` is in use and holds `v`.

### `slots_full`

```bastio
spec fn slots_full[V](s: &Slots[V], lo: u64, hi: u64) -> bool {
  forall k: u64 :: lo <= k && k < hi ==> slots_has[V](s, k)
}
```

Every slot of `lo..hi` is in use (slots past the end count as free).

### `slots_same_but`

```bastio
spec fn slots_same_but[V](s: &Slots[V], o: &Slots[V], at: u64) -> bool {
  vlen(o.vals) <= vlen(s.vals)
    && (forall k: u64 :: k < vlen(o.vals) && k != at ==> vget(s.vals, k) == vget(o.vals, k))
    && (forall k: u64 :: vlen(o.vals) <= k && k < vlen(s.vals) && k != at ==> vget(s.vals, k) is Option::None)
}
```

`s` agrees with `o` on every slot but `at`: a slot of either that exists
in the other holds the same thing, and the slots in use are the same.
